text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thursday:
- Over 12,000 people sought asylum in Switzerland in the first seven months of 1997, some 30 percent more than in the same period last year.
- Switzerland's Telecom PTT is expanding its business in Austria, where its newly-established headquarters in Vienna will offer telecommunications services for mid-sized and large companies.
- St Gall's Cantonal bank reported first-half gross profit up 32.2 percent at 72.9 million Swiss francs compared to the first half of 1996.
-Swiss watch exports rose by 7.8 percent to 3.857 billion Swiss francs in the first half of 1997. Swiss watch sales in the U.S. increased by 15.8 percent thanks to the stronger dollar.
-Transport group Kuehne & Nagel in Schindellegi is taking over the distribution activities of U.S. chemical and energy group DuPont in Europe, the middle East and Africa.
-Swiss publishing company Ringier announced it is creating a new magazine. Named "Cashual", the monthly will be geared towards younger readers and should be on the market by next spring.

-Andreas Haenggi, Director of the Nestle factory in Guatemala, and his 22-year-old son Nicolas were arrested in Antigua on Tuesday for allegedly being involved with drug dealing. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
